justification: Changes what two outreach claims assert and what gates them, plus evidence text on three config entries. No production write, no change to what any property is served: scope_evidence is data the checks read, the tagger does not. Not Critical because nothing served moves; not Minor because a wrong gate here would let outreach claim something false.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: Measured on this branch, each mutation run against hand-built fixture worlds whose correct answer is fixed in the test, not produced by the code: M1 dropping the under-listing comparison -> 1 failed/10 passed; M2 ignoring stated exceptions -> 3 failed/8 passed; M3 disabling the check that the per-council split sums to DQ-114's own total -> 1 failed/10 passed. Clean: 11 passed.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: The list is computed from regulatory_provisions via DQ-114's own SQL (dq_probe_live.PROBES) and dq_probe_applicability_config.probe_115; the moved scope sentences were checked against the council PDFs by dq_probe_scope_evidence_fidelity.py (all spans OK).
falsifiable_check.observed_red: pytest printed '1 failed, 10 passed' (M1: test_underclaim_fails), '3 failed, 8 passed' (M2: test_matching_list_passes_and_exception_excuses_its_rows, test_without_the_exception..., test_stale...), '1 failed, 10 passed' (M3: test_split_drifting_from_dq114_fails); restored file printed '11 passed'. Before the fix the real gate printed 'OC-17: FAILS' with DQ-114 23 and DQ-115 47.

pre_impl.existing_data: regulatory_provisions served set (is_current AND v2_is_actionable): 18 source_council slugs, all joined to lga_registry.display_name. DQ-114 = 23 keys in 6 (council, chapter, key) groups. COUNCIL_CONFIGS aliases share dicts, so attribution is by identity.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: If DQ-114's query changes and the split does not, the totals disagree and the check FAILS rather than listing on a stale split. A DQ-115 hit in a config no served council uses also FAILS rather than being dropped.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Read-only. Applies to whatever the database holds at run time; the published JSON must be re-matched whenever a council starts or stops passing.

functions.name: outreach_scoped_councils.check
functions.if_none: unreadable JSON -> FAIL; unreachable DB -> UNKNOWN, never PASS

values.value: dq_check --outreach 17 of 17; DQ-115 47 -> 41; pytest 7674 passed; jest 108 suites/1503 tests

queries.where_clause: is_current AND v2_is_actionable AND source_council IS NOT NULL AND source IN undetermined list OR NULL
queries.if_zero: no council delisted by DQ-114; a stated exception then reads stale and FAILS
queries.if_wrong: sum is compared with DQ-114's own count; disagreement FAILS

break_it.scenario: A council is published that has an undecided key
break_it.what_happens: the page overclaims a council that still has an undecided key

break_it.scenario: A council starts passing but is not published
break_it.what_happens: the page silently understates which councils the claim covers

break_it.scenario: The stated Canterbury exception stops matching rows after a retag
break_it.what_happens: page states an exception that no longer exists

break_it.scenario: Fleet-wide sub-check fails in one council
break_it.what_happens: the claim could name a council that a fleet-wide check fails in
break_it.how: those sub-checks stay fleet-wide in OC-17; any failure fails the claim outright
